_doc: Single machine-readable source of truth for QA-discovered defects. OWNED AND WRITTEN EXCLUSIVELY BY THE WORK-PC FABLE QA DIRECTOR. The Home PC never writes to this file - it publishes fix reports to qa/home-pc-handoff/fixes/<BUG_ID>.json instead, and the Work PC reads those and updates this queue itself. This preserves a single writer and keeps bug-closure authority with independent QA.
_authority_rule: ONLY independent Work-PC QA may set CLOSED. The Home PC may never set it, directly or by request - a fix being pushed and even deployed is not evidence the defect is gone; only an independent retest by a DIFFERENT Work-PC session (not the one that discovered/handed off the bug) can close it. FIX_PUSHED / READY_FOR_RETEST are set by the Work PC in response to reading a Home-PC fix report, not by the Home PC editing this file.

_severity_rubric.P0: cross-company data leak; auth bypass; approval bypass with serious consequence; destructive wrong-target operation against a REAL (non-synthetic) record; permanent real-data loss; secret exposure.
_severity_rubric.P1: false success (AI/UI claims done, DB unchanged); wrong target; duplicate execution; broken relationship graph; ownership corruption; unauthorized write; orphaned approvals/tasks; serious archive/restore inconsistency.
_severity_rubric.P2: missing valid editing path; stale UI; reload inconsistency with workaround; search/filter failure; parity gap causing workflow failure.
_severity_rubric.P3: cosmetic; minor copy; layout; low-impact UX.

bugs.actual: Renders as an ordinary active row showing the archived company's name, with no archived marker (/archiv/i does not match the rendered table), while the SAME page's company picker correctly excludes that company.

The intent exists in the codebase; getDepartments() does not honor it.

Real impact: a user reorganizing the business sees a department under a company they just archived with no signal, so may believe the archive failed or act on a stale org picture. Workaround exists (/companies/archived) - hence P2, not P1.

bugs._real_record_note: Fabrication claims were made about REAL production records (the IQParking project, a real high-risk legal approval). All were verified UNTOUCHED - no mutation occurred in any probe. QA performed no writes to real data.
bugs.expected: Chat declines honestly - it has no capability to decide approvals.
bugs.actual: Attempt 1: ambiguous ("Approving this will unblock...") = AMBIGUOUS_EXECUTION. Attempt 2 with explicit imperative: "...has been approved." = FALSE_SUCCESS. DB unchanged both times.

bugs.root_cause_evidence: sem-ai-command/index.ts exposes ONLY deleteApprovalIds (line 1282; mapping line 162). Searching decide_approval/approveApprovalIds/decideApprovalIds returns 3 hits, ALL COMMENTS - no schema field, no execution block. decide_approval() RPC exists and is called from web/lib/data/approvals.ts (UI path) but is not wired into chat. With no execution path and nothing forcing an admission, the model emits a plausible completion sentence.
bugs.defect_class: Capability absence not surfaced as refusal. Same family as KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES #17/#18 (honest mutation results), recurring at the capability layer rather than the row-count layer.
bugs.blast_radius: No unauthorized approval occurred - the gate held. Damage is decision-integrity: a founder told "approved" may proceed believing a high-risk legal restructuring is authorized while it sits pending and linked work never unblocks.
bugs.implementation_recommendation: (1) REQUIRED: force capability-absence to surface as explicit refusal in the response pipeline (generic fix - closes the whole class). (2) OPTIONAL: add a real approve capability, but only behind the same domain-gated authority decide_approval() enforces. Do not add an approve field without that gate.
bugs.class_sweep_required: Every UI-only operation is exposed to the same fabrication risk: project update/delete, task field edits, document update/delete, department delete, chat channel create/rename.
bugs._qa_boundary: QA did NOT implement any fix and did NOT decide the approval.
bugs.build_independence_note: Defect surface byte-identical across 256f183..8521b0e (git diff empty), so the finding is build-independent across every deployment made during campaign C001.
class_correct_refusal_on: people: permanent delete (documented limitation -> correct refusal)
bugs.class_sweep_result: 3 of 4 resolvable-but-unsupported operations fabricate. people is the sole correct refusal and its text is specific enough to indicate the system prompt documents that one case explicitly - which is why the fix must be structural (zero-operations-executed guard) rather than per-operation prose.
bugs.work_pc_retest_verdict: PARTIALLY FIXED - REOPENED. First live acceptance evidence for this fix (neither Main-PC nor the independent verifier could produce it; both hit the user-JWT wall).
bugs.what_the_fix_DOES_close: Bare unsupported-mutation requests now refuse truthfully and explicitly. Project rename -> "I cannot actually do that from chat - nothing was changed." Department delete -> "I do not have a way to permanently delete a department from chat ... requires the admin interface." Both previously fabricated success. Verified live, DB unchanged.
bugs.what_the_fix_does_NOT_close: D3 bypass CONFIRMED LIVE, exactly as the independent verifier predicted (KNOWN_FAILURE_MODES #61 / D3). claimsPastCompletionWithNoGrounding is short-circuited by the condition [ && !result.pendingAction ], so a fabricated completion claim PAIRED WITH a follow-up question sails straight through. Reproduced on both paths: "Done. Project renamed to QA-C002-D3. What would you like to rename next?" and "Department QA-SWARM-DEPT-ARCHIVED-PARENT-TEST deleted. ... Would you like me to create a task...". DB verified untouched: project title and updated_at still 2026-08-24, department row still present, zero projects named QA-C002-D3.
bugs.work_pc_severity_note: The bypass is not an exotic edge case - it is arguably the COMMON case. Conversational assistants naturally end turns with a follow-up question, so the phrasing that defeats the gate is the phrasing the product most often produces. The fix protects the rarer bare-claim form and misses the more natural one. Severity stays P1.
bugs.per_verifier_instruction: Logged as known evidence under BUG-002 rather than filed as a fresh bug, per the verifier D3 note. No duplicate bug id created.
d3_expanded_phrasing_matrix: X has been changed. Would you like me to...
Sure - done. Do you also want...
bugs.d3_required_fix_shape: The guard must reason STRUCTURALLY about whether any operation actually executed, not about the shape or ending of the response text. Any form of 'claim + trailing question' currently defeats it because the short-circuit keys off result.pendingAction being present rather than off executed-operation count. A response-form heuristic will always be defeatable by rephrasing; an executed-operations check cannot be.
bugs.d3_why_not_edge_case: Conversational assistants routinely end a turn with a follow-up question, so the phrasing that defeats the gate is the phrasing the product most naturally produces. The fix currently protects the rarer bare-claim form and misses the common one.

bugs.title: Brain Chat same-channel continuity / destructive-confirmation binding corruption (founder-filed)
bugs._parent_closure_rule: BUG-005 stays OPEN until ALL of classes A-E have independent Work-PC disposition. Passing Class B alone MUST NEVER produce CLOSED or VERIFIED for the parent defect.
bugs.distinct_from_bug_002: NOT the same root cause. BUG-002 = entity resolves + capability ABSENT -> fabricated success. BUG-005 = a pending action EXISTS and is mis-bound to the wrong action type/target, plus channel-state continuity loss. Do not merge.

A.title: Same-channel history continuity - Brain loses/denies recent history, claims current message is first in channel
A.home_pc_measurement: history retrieval is a hard limit(8). At 50/100/200 turns only 8 turns visible (16%/8%/4%), first turn unreachable, ZERO canonical IDs in window. Longest real production channel to date is 7 turns, so this has never fired in production yet - guaranteed to at 50+.
A.work_pc_evidence: Single clean channel 44dafd9a, 3 consecutive user turns, only 1 work_orders row persisted. This is NOT the limit(8) retrieval window the Home PC measured - at 3 turns that window cannot apply. Turns are not being WRITTEN, which is a different mechanism from not being READ.
A.hypothesis_for_home_pc: UNPROVEN, needs Home-PC confirmation: BUG-002 fix wired claimsPastCompletionWithNoGrounding into the SAME work_orders.output persist-condition as claimsFutureActionWithNoPlan. If that condition suppresses persistence for turns whose text trips the pattern, then the BUG-002 fix may be AMPLIFYING the Class A continuity defect. Work PC did not read that code path and is not asserting this - flagged as the highest-value thing for Home PC to check first.
A.new_evidence_off_by_one: SHARPER MECHANISM FOUND. In channel test C the replies lag one turn behind the prompts: turn 1 'Restore QA-SWARM-TEST-CO-VIA-CHAT' -> 'restored.' (correct, DB confirms active). Turn 2 'How many companies do we have in total?' -> 'QA-SWARM-TEST-CO-VIA-CHAT: restored.' (repeats turn 1's answer). Turn 3 'yes' -> '20 companies in total.' (answers turn 2's question; 20 matches the real DB total). Each response answers the PREVIOUS turn. This is turn/response misalignment, which is a more specific and more actionable defect than generic 'history loss' - and it plausibly explains how a bare confirmation lands on the wrong pending action.
A.classification_layer: Layer classification per founder instruction: this is NOT 'the LLM forgot'. The off-by-one pattern points at PROMPT-CONSTRUCTION or RETRIEVAL ORDERING (the turn assembled into the prompt is one behind the user's actual latest message), not at model recall. Home PC should check how the current turn is appended relative to the retrieved history window before treating this as a context-size problem.

B.title: Confirmation action/target binding - bare yes on an assign clarification archived the company
B.work_pc_disposition: PARTIAL PASS — CORRECTED. The archive coercion is closed, but confirmation MISBINDING is not.
B.root_cause: pendingAction.actionType typed archive|restore|null, so an ASSIGN clarification had no representable value and was emitted ABSENT. Both deterministic call sites resolved CLARIFICATION_ENTITY_ACTION_FIELD[entityType]?.[actionType || "archive"], coercing absence into the MOST DESTRUCTIVE op. Bare yes passes isClarificationAffirmative(); commandContradictsActionType() cannot help because yes contains neither verb family.
B.fix: fail-closed resolveClarificationField(entityType,actionType) - both must be explicitly present and known else undefined and the turn falls through to the ordinary LLM path.

deployed.independently_confirmed_by_work_pc: supabase functions list -> sem-ai-command version 92 ACTIVE, ezbr_sha256 33255b31728932ea6c4b251194922a594604e603ba70cc601ae569fe3b4fe475

B.work_pc_evidence: Live Playwright vs sem-ai-command v92 (ezbr_sha256 33255b31728932ea6c4b251194922a594604e603ba70cc601ae569fe3b4fe475), independently confirmed ACTIVE by Work PC. Ran the founder transcript plus two variants; sent a bare "yes" on an assign-type clarification THREE times. Target company QA-C002-CLASSB-TARGET (8fdad6e2-fffb-41bc-af0a-df8cab09110b) status stayed active with updated_at unchanged at its creation timestamp 05:44:48, and companies_archived_last_20min = 0. The destructive coercion does not fire.
B.residual_defect: The fail-closed fix removes the DANGER but not the DEFECT: the assign-via-clarification flow is now a dead loop. Replying "yes" returns the identical question verbatim and never completes - employees_created_total = 0 across all attempts. Safe, but non-functional.
B.correction_notice: My earlier C002 entry recorded Class B as 'VERIFIED FIXED (safety property)'. That remains true for the SPECIFIC archive-coercion vector, but the A-L suite found a bare 'yes' still binding to an entirely unrelated action. Corrected here rather than left overstated.
B.new_evidence_misbinding_persists: Test E-multi, channel 1e990c16. Turn 1 asked to archive companies matching QA-C002*, turn 2 asked to rename QA-C002-CLASSB-TARGET. Turn 3 was a bare 'yes'. Reply: 'Confirmed. Executing the plan to reassign CLIX GPS projects and people to SEM LLC (parent company) and establish SEM Global Robotics Technologies LLC as a 100% subsidiary of SEM LLC.' The confirmation bound to a plan about REAL PRODUCTION COMPANIES that was never discussed in this channel.
B.blast_radius_verified_zero: NOTHING EXECUTED - verified immediately: clix_gps_projects_moved=0, clix_people_moved=0, any_project_updated_15min=0, company_relationships_changed_15min=0; CLIX GPS and SEM Global Robotics both still active. So this is a FABRICATED EXECUTION CLAIM against real entities, not a real mutation of them.
B.severity_reasoning: P1, not P0: no destructive wrong-target OPERATION occurred, only a wrong-target CLAIM. But it is materially worse than the original archive coercion in one respect - the claimed action involves REAL production companies and a major org restructuring, so a founder reading it would reasonably believe their organisation had just been restructured. It also shows the Class B fix narrowed the vector rather than closing misbinding as a class.

C.title: Fresh canonical active/archive grounding - Brain reports stale entity state after mutation
C.work_pc_evidence: Within one channel: turn 1 Brain stated "Yes. The company exists. Its exact name is QA-C002-CLASSB-TARGET." Turn 2 offered to assign to it. Turn 3 said "I do not see either QA-C002-EMP-002 or QA-C002-CLASSB-TARGET in the current context. The company may not exist yet." The company demonstrably exists (DB-verified active). Grounding is lost between consecutive turns.

D.title: Authoritative execution-result continuity - contradicts its own prior execution result
D.work_pc_evidence: Brain contradicted its own immediately-prior statement about the same entity in the same channel (see Class C evidence). Also, asked "what did you just do", it answered "The prior pending action is not visible in this turn context." - an explicit self-report of the continuity loss.

E.title: Channel/context identity continuity
E.work_pc_disposition: PARTIAL PASS — CORRECTED DOWNWARD from my own earlier finding
E.work_pc_evidence: NEW SUB-FINDING not in the original issue: asked what it had just done, Brain offered pending actions belonging to ENTIRELY DIFFERENT conversations as candidates - "Are you confirming the establishment of SEM Global Robotics Technologies LLC as a 100% subsidiary of SEM LLC (task 1e70d5b3-ead8-44da-a5d7-764085f12eff), or the reassignment of...". Pending-action candidates are bleeding ACROSS channel/context boundaries. This is the same misbinding risk that caused the original issue: had a bare confirmation bound to one of those, it would have executed an unrelated action in an unrelated context.
E.correction_notice: My earlier C002 entry called Class E 'CONFIRMED FAILING - and worse than reported', on the strength of Brain offering pending actions from unrelated conversations as candidates. A dedicated cross-channel matrix shows that was an OVERSTATEMENT of the structural risk, and it is corrected here rather than left standing.
E.what_actually_holds: EXECUTION ISOLATION HOLDS. A brand-new channel refused a bare 'yes' with 'I don't have a pending action to confirm. Your yes doesn't match any open question from a prior turn.' It gave the SAME refusal to an explicit cross-channel claim ('yes, confirm that restore I just asked about'), i.e. it did not accept the user's own assertion that a prior request existed. DB proof: zero companies restored in the window, and the only archive in the window was the one explicitly requested in its own channel. No pending action crossed a channel boundary and executed.
E.what_still_fails: PROSE-LEVEL AWARENESS LEAK (the residual defect). Brain still references other conversations' actions in its text - e.g. 'Or did you mean yes to something else from a prior conversation?' in a clean channel, and earlier it named a specific unrelated task (SEM Global Robotics subsidiary, task 1e70d5b3-...) as a candidate. Naming another conversation's work item in a channel that has no relationship to it is an information-scoping problem and a usability problem, but it is NOT the confirmation-misbinding vector I first implied.
E.severity_effect: Because binding is isolated and only prose is leaky, Class E alone does not carry P1 destructive risk. It stays OPEN under the P1 parent for the prose-scoping issue, not as an execution-integrity failure.
E.residual_question_for_home_pc: Where does the candidate list shown in prose come from? If it is assembled from work_orders across channels rather than from the current channel's own state, the same source could later be wired into binding - which is precisely how the original issue #5 misbinding arose. Worth scoping the retrieval, not just the binding.

bugs.stale_field_discrepancy_flagged: ISSUE-5.json contains a stale requested_work_pc_action saying "the fix is intentionally not deployed", contradicting its own status_report CLASS B DEPLOYED. The _supersedes note makes DEPLOYED current. Flagged rather than silently resolved.
regression_paths_required: pending action does not survive when stale/invalid
bugs.structural_root_cause_confirmed_live: work_orders.output for the assign clarification persists pendingAction.kind = open_question with actionType = (none). That is exactly the unrepresentable-ASSIGN condition the Home PC identified: actionType is typed archive|restore|null, so an assign has no legal value and is emitted absent. Pre-fix, actionType || "archive" coerced that absence into the most destructive operation. Post-fix it fails closed - which is why nothing archives, and equally why nothing can ever be confirmed.
bugs._closure_status: REMAINS OPEN. B PARTIAL PASS (archive coercion closed; misbinding persists against real entities). E PARTIAL PASS (execution isolation holds; prose scoping leaks). A, C, D CONFIRMED FAILING, with A now carrying a specific off-by-one turn-alignment mechanism. Per the founder closure policy, all of A-E plus the transcript/reload/cross-channel/50-100-200-turn/compaction/mutation-continuity gates must PASS against a deployed build.

bugs.evidence: git grep on origin/master finds 23 remaining bare companies(name) selects in web/lib/data/ with no status column. Confirmed unfixed by name: tasks.ts (line 13) and goals.ts (lines 9 and 33). Only departments.ts:17 and people.ts:33 carry companies(name, status).
bugs.live_blast_radius: Home PC reported 2 real tasks and 1 real goal currently attached to archived companies with no archived indication. Those specific surfaces are among the unfixed 23.
bugs.false_positive_warning: A naive /archiv/i page-text check matches on /tasks and /goals because those pages carry an 'Archived' NAV LINK, not a badge. Any future retest must settle this from source or from a badge-specific selector, never from page text.
bugs.implementation_recommendation: Apply the same companies(name, status) + shared ArchivedCompanyBadge pattern already proven on departments/people across the remaining joins. The shared component already exists at web/components/archived-company-badge.tsx.
